newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Banks and properties lead Singapore shares lower.
newsitem.headline: Banks and properties lead Singapore shares lower.

text.p: Singapore shares ended lower on Monday led by falls in banks and property stocks.
Dealers said investor focus was on Malaysian over the counter shares which registered good gains sending the UOB OTC index up by 7.96 points to end at 1,286.65.

But Singapore shares were mostly softer. "The banks and property counters came off. There is no reason except that they had a good run up over the last few weeks and it is time to take some profit," said a dealer with foreign brokerage.
Losers included City Developments, SPH foreign, DBS foreign and OUB foreign, down between Singapore 60 and 20 cents each.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrial index ended 17.36 points lower to 2,225.35. Total market volume was 298 million units with 193 gainers against 198 losers.

Door maker Chuan Soon Huat was heavily traded and fell 2.5 cents to S$0.57. Dealers could give no reason for the volume but noted the closing price was still at a premium over its initial public offer price of S$0.35.
Liquid crystal electronic products maker IDT Holdings, which started trading today, ended at US$0.885 against its IPO price of US$0.73. -Doreen Siow 65-8703092 REUTER
